title: Flowise Python code validator -- T1027 mathematical bold Unicode homoglyphs slip past an ASCII-only word-boundary blacklist
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-70470 (GHSA-52fh-8v99-63c2),
affecting `validatePythonCodeForDataFrame` in
`pythonCodeValidator.ts`, which gates every call to
`pyodide.runPythonAsync` in `CSVAgent` and `AirtableAgent`.

The validator is a regex blacklist using `\b__class__\b`-style
patterns. JavaScript's `\b` word boundary is computed against the
ASCII word class only, so a Unicode letter such as U+1D41A
(mathematical bold small a) is treated as a non-word character and
never matches. Python 3 (PEP 3131) NFKC-normalizes every identifier
at parse time, so `__cl𝐚ss__` parses identically to `__class__`. The
attacker writes `obj.__cl𝐚ss__.__b𝐚se__.__subcl𝐚sses__()` to reach
`catch_warnings`, then assembles `__import__` from `chr()` calls to
dodge the literal-string blacklist entries, obtains the `js` module,
and calls `child_process.execSync` on the host -- reopening the exact
RCE class two prior advisories (GHSA-3hjv-c53m-58jj,
GHSA-v38x-c887-992f) patched, because both patches relied entirely on
this bypassable validator.

Detection logic flags Python source submitted to the CSVAgent /
AirtableAgent code path containing a dunder-style identifier
(`__word__`) where at least one character is outside the ASCII range
-- the exact homoglyph-substitution shape this advisory's proof of
concept confirms the validator's `\b`-anchored regex cannot see.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (FlowiseAI, via
GHSA, citing the exact validator source file, the ASCII-only `\b`
root cause, PEP 3131 NFKC normalization as the mechanism, and a
runnable proof of concept confirming `validate() === true` on the
malicious payload before it achieves host RCE), fixed in Flowise 3.1.3 (verified via live GHSA lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the rule's original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this note corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
